entries.name: Google Cloud Video Intelligence (logo + text detection)
corrections: Official page fetched raw via curl: Logo detection and Text detection are each $0.15/min after the first 1,000 min free (table shows 0-1,001 free, then $0.15). Partial minutes rounded up; 'over 100,000 min/month, contact sales' confirmed.

The $0.135 and $0.12 are NOT volume tiers: they are the 'Gemini Enterprise Flexible Savings Plan - 1 Year' ($0.135) and '- 3 Year' ($0.12) columns for the same >1,000 min band. Replace the 'unconfirmed page variant' wording.
Arithmetic: 0.15 x 60 = $9.00/hr; x100,000 h = $900,000. 1-yr plan 0.135 x 60 = $8.10; 3-yr 0.12 x 60 = $7.20. Logo + text both: $18.00/hr. Free 1,000 min is negligible at this volume.

evidence.quote: Text detection 0 minute to 1,001 minute $0.00 (Free) 1,001 minute and above $0.15 ... $0.135 ... $0.12 | Logo detection ... $0.15 ... $0.135 ... $0.12 (columns: Price; Flexible Savings Plan 1 Year; 3 Year)

entries.name: Amazon Rekognition (video labels / image DetectText / Custom Labels)
corrections: WRONG: entry says the $0.10/min stored-video rate is 'label detection, not OCR'. The AWS page's Stored video table lists Label Detection, Content Moderation, Text Detection, Face Detection, Celebrity Recognition, Face Search, Person Pathing all against the same archived-video price token; the Price List SKU (USE1-MinsOfArchVideoProcessed) is $0.10/min and its description names LabelDetection/FaceDetection/PersonTracking/CelebrityRecognition/ContentModeration/FaceSearch (text not named in the SKU string, but the page maps Text Detection to it and the free tier covers Text Detection). So stored-video text detection = $0.10/min. No logo-detection API exists in the list.

DetectText is Image 'Group 2' (async SKU same tiers): $0.0010 first 1M images/month, $0.0008 next 4M (1M-5M), $0.0006 next 30M (5M-35M), $0.00025 over 35M. Entry only had first tier; lower tiers were 'not retrieved'.
Custom Labels verified: inference 0.0666667/min = $4.00/hr, training 0.0166667/min = $1.00/hr, billed per model-hour with 1 min minimum (not per video hour; throughput dependent).

Streaming: Price List has two live SKUs: $0.12/min and $0.00817/min; entry lists only $0.00817 and which product each belongs to was not confirmed. Page lists streaming video events with Label Detection and Face Search. Treat as unverified.
Our 1 fps assumption is not AWS's; AWS example pages do not define frames per minute.

evidence.quote: USE1-MinsOfArchVideoProcessed 0.1000000000 Minutes Processed; USE1-Group2-AsyncImagesProcessed 0-1M 0.001, 1M-5M 0.0008, 5M-35M 0.0006, 35M-Inf 0.00025; USE1-inferenceminutes 0.06666667; USE1-minutestrained 0.01666667

Group 2: DetectFaces, DetectModerationLabels, DetectLabels, DetectText, RecognizeCelebrities, DetectProtectiveEquipment APIs ... Stored video: Label Detection / Content Moderation / Text Detection / Face Detection ... /min ... Free Tier ... covers ... Text Detection

entries.name: Twelve Labs
corrections: Raw page confirms: 'Video indexing (one time) $2.50 / hour' (listed under Search/Marengo), 'Embedding Infra (Monthly) $0.09 / hour', Search API $4 / 1000 queries; Analyze API (Pegasus 1.6 / 1.5) 'Input video $1.75 / hour', 'Input image $3 / 1M tokens', 'Output tokens $7.5 / 1M tokens'. Units: per hour of video.

The $4.25/hr sum (2.50 + 1.75) is not supported by the page: indexing sits under the Search/Marengo table and the Analyze table lists input video separately; the page does not say Pegasus analysis requires paying indexing as well. Treat $1.75/hr (= $175,000 per 100k h) as analysis input only, plus output tokens at $7.5/1M; indexing-only $2.50/hr = $250,000.
Which Pegasus version the $1.75 belongs to (1.6 vs 1.5 tabs) is not distinguishable in the extracted text.

evidence.quote: Video indexing (one time) Free $2.50 / hour ... Analyze API Pegasus 1.6 Pegasus 1.5 Input video Free $1.75 / hour Custom Input image Free $3 / 1M tokens Output tokens Free $7.5 / 1M tokens

entries.name: Roboflow hosted inference
corrections: Rate wrong: official Model pricing page gives RF-DETR Small = 0.1875 credits per 1,000 images (Nano 0.125; XL 0.25), not 0.2. Standard rate applies to first 250,000 images/month.

'1 credit = 500 s inference' is wrong context: official docs say 500 execution seconds per credit applies only to custom Python blocks and vision-language-model blocks, not detection models, which are billed per image.

Dollar per credit IS on an official page (roboflow.com/pricing, Core plan): $3.90/credit (20 credits, $39/mo) falling to $2.86/credit (500 credits, $1,399/mo); free tier 10 credits/mo. Entry's '~$4' and '~$3 annual' were third-party; $4 overstated.

Volume discounts (graduated, workspace-wide: 25% off 250K-500K, 50% 500K-1M, 60% 1M-2M, 70% 2M-5M, 80% over 5M) were omitted. At 360M images/month RF-DETR Small = about 13,685 credits = $53,372 at $3.90 or $39,140 at $2.86 per 100k h (~$0.53 / $0.39 per hour); credit packs at that scale would be an enterprise contract so treat as indicative.
'Cold starts 2.2 credits/1,000' not found on the official pages read; unverified.

evidence.quote: RF-DETR * Nano: 0.125 * Small, Base, Medium, Large: 0.1875 * XL: 0.25 ... Over 5M 80% off
+10 credits a month, $39 a month, 20 credits in total $3.90/credit ... +490 credits a month, $1,399 a month, 500 credits in total $2.86/credit
Custom Python blocks and vision language models are billed for the time they run, at 500 execution seconds per credit.
